<reflection>
After two experiments, the NLL values show that M20 is a clear outlier (much higher NLL), while M4 and M5 are also relatively poor fits. However, a large group of mechanisms (M8, M6, M2, M3, M13, M7, M15, M12, M9, M11, M19, M1, M10, M18, M17, M14, M16) have NLLs within a narrow range (difference <1.35), meaning they are all still plausible. The second experiment (low catalyst) shifted rankings, making M8 and M6 the best, but did not sufficiently discriminate among the group. The aim of the second turn was to probe catalyst concentration dependence, which was achieved but further discrimination is needed.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
To further discriminate among the remaining mechanisms, we propose an experiment with high catalyst concentration (0.1 M) and moderate initial product (0.2 M), while keeping substrate at 2.0 M. High catalyst will amplify effects of catalyst dimerization (M2, M3, M5, M13, M18, M19) and other bimolecular catalyst steps. The presence of product will test reversibility of the product formation step and product inhibition (M12, M17). This condition is orthogonal to previous runs (which had no product and lower catalyst) and avoids extreme saturation or depletion. It should yield distinct kinetic profiles for mechanisms with catalyst-catalyst interactions versus those without, and for mechanisms sensitive to product concentration. This design aims to reduce uncertainty across many mechanisms simultaneously, rather than focusing on a single pair.
</hypothesis>
